title: Kota Actions is Live: Make Changes Across Your Entire Instance at Once
summary: Stop editing one at a time. Kota can now make changes across everything in your Hyperbound instance, at one time, from wherever you work.
body_markdown:
Your CRO pulls up the funnel and discovery to demo has been slipping. He thinks he knows why it's been slipping recently. Reps are feature dumping, pitching before they understand what the prospect actually needs.


So the ask lands on you. Every scorecard needs to grade for it. Every rep needs somewhere to practice not doing it.


Here is what that used to cost.


You have scorecards for cold calls, discovery, demos, negotiation. Split by product line, by vertical, by region. You open the first one, add the criterion, write the grading prompt, publish. Then the second. Then the twelfth. Then you start on the bots, one at a time, for every vertical your team sells into and every language they sell in.


Most teams don't finish. They pick the two scorecards that matter most, build three bots, and call it a rollout. Not because the work is hard, but because there is so much of it.


Kota Actions is what changes that.


‍


‍


## Ask once


Open Kota and describe what you want:


> Update all our scorecards to add a criteria that checks for feature dumping.


Kota pulls the set, shows you every scorecard it matched, and waits. You confirm. It applies the change to all of them at the same time and comes back with a diff of exactly what moved on each one: the criterion it added, the grading prompt it wrote, the criteria count going up by one.


Nothing is live yet. You read the diff, then publish.


Then the practice side, same idea:


> Create discovery call bots to test reps on feature dumping. Create variations of them for English, Spanish, German, Korean, and Japanese.


You describe the shape of what you need instead of listing what you want built. Kota generates the set, asks which folder and which scorecard should grade them, and publishes when you say so. The bots come back live, ready to take a call.


Two requests. A rollout that would have taken a week of forms.


‍


## It works on everything, not just these two


Bots and scorecards are the obvious ones. Learning modules and competitions work the same way. Create one, create fifty, edit one, edit all of them.


The pattern holds regardless of what you are changing: describe the outcome and the scope, review what Kota drafted, publish. You are not learning a new interface. It is the same Kota you already ask about your calls and your pipeline, and it can now do the work instead of telling you where to click.


‍


## And it works wherever you already are


Kota Actions runs in Hyperbound, in Slack, and in any MCP client your team has open.


‍


‍


Requests reach you everywhere. A manager pings you in a channel asking for a variant for their team. A CRO forwards you a call recording. You are three tabs deep in something else when you realize the Mid-Market scorecard needs the same criterion the Enterprise one just got.


‍


‍


None of that arrives in Hyperbound, so none of it should require opening Hyperbound. Handle it in the thread where it landed.


‍


## Nothing publishes without you


Every action is scoped, confirmed, and reversible.


Kota tells you what it matched before it touches anything. Changes come back as drafts. Every draft carries a diff showing what was added, removed, or reworded. You publish, keep them as drafts, or tell Kota to try again.


Actions only reach objects inside Hyperbound. Nothing writes to a downstream system.


‍


## The part that actually changes


The reason enablement teams cap what they attempt has never been the difficulty of the work. It is the volume. Adding one criterion is a minute. Adding it everywhere it belongs is a project nobody schedules, so it doesn't happen, and the program ships narrower than it should have.


That constraint is gone. Not because building got easier, but because the number of things you are building stopped mattering.


‍


## Available now


Kota Actions is live in your Hyperbound instance today. Open Kota and ask it to build or change something, whether that is one record or every one you have.


If your team already uses Kota in Slack or through MCP, it works there too, with no additional setup.


‍
